prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1353; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is not named on the policy and does not live with the policyholder.
text:
Entry 1: Insured reported a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection and stated the claimant's vehicle was stopped in front of them at the time of impact. Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact has been routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Photos submitted by the insured show the rear bumper, tail lamp assembly, and trunk lid damage, which is largely consistent with the impact described. No independent witnesses have come forward at this stage.

Entry 3: Claimant's attorney provided the initial injury notice, reporting a concussion diagnosed at the emergency department. The reported injury appears consistent with the kind and force of a collision of this type.

Entry 4: Reviewed the prior-records request. No earlier injury to the same body area is on file, and no prior claims involving the claimant's vehicle have been identified.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed the account given in the first notice. The claimant has described the events the same way in each conversation so far.

Entry 6: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for a concussion of this severity, and the treating physician's notes explain the extended follow-up. Requested updated records to confirm the current plan of care.

Entry 7: Claimant's seating position at the moment of impact is still not fully clear from the statements so far. Following up with the attorney to clarify before any evaluation is finalized.

Entry 8: Confirmed with the insured that the driver involved is not listed on the policy and does not reside with the policyholder. Coverage questions are being reviewed under the policy terms.

Entry 9: Reviewed the vehicle repair estimate and the inspection notes. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the policy's effective date, and no earlier damage to the vehicle has been identified.

Entry 10: File remains open pending the updated medical records, the outstanding seating-position clarification, and a final coverage determination on the driver's status.
